items.title: A lot of people have been dunking on gemini 3.6 flash since it dropped.
items.summary:
A lot of people have been dunking on gemini 3.6 flash since it dropped.

The claim: it didn’t get smarter on any level.

That part’s actually true, considering it scores a 50 on the intelligence index, exact same as 3.5 flash, with no iq gain.

But as someone who runs automations on flash tier models, & also use it as a fallback on Hermes; intelligence was never the thing holding those back.

What actually matters when a model’s running a task 200 times an hour is speed, cost per run, & whether it reliably calls the right tool.

& that’s exactly what they’ve moved:

➥ osworld-verified jumped to 83% from 78.4.

➥ output tokens dropped hard on deepswe, with fewer loops.

➥ cheaper per task, & not just per token.

So is it a smarter model? 
Maybe not.

Plus they’ve also fallen behind on the top 5 labs.

But it’s a cheaper, faster, more reliable worker for agents, and maybe that’s the upgrade that actually counts, & not another point on a benchmark chart.

Not saying the crowd is wrong to care about that.

Just the wrong lens for what this release might’ve actually been built for.

That said.

The flash drops are clearly filler while gemini 3.5 pro sits stuck in training.

But they’ve also announced pretraining for gemini 4 & they’re calling it their most ambitious run yet.

So just maybe they’re not completely cooked yet.

Curious to know what everyone else is running their flash tier models for.

items.title: Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June.
items.summary:
Google promised Gemini 3.5 Pro in June.

June passed. July came and is going already. 

As of July 21 Google’s public position is that Gemini 3.5 Pro is “currently testing with partners” with no confirmed release date.

Bloomberg and other outlets have reported that Gemini 3.5 Pro is behind schedule, with Google pushing back its launch window, though Google has not publicly blamed specific coding performance failures.

Meanwhile Google shipped Gemini 3.6 Flash on July 21, along with 3.5 Flash-Lite and a restricted cybersecurity model called 3.5 Flash Cyber. Faster and cheaper, but still not the flagship Pro model developers have been waiting on since May.

The current live Pro model in Google’s lineup remains Gemini 3.1 Pro.

If you have been holding off on building something while waiting for 3.5 Pro, stop waiting. There is no confirmed date. Build with what is available today.

items.title: JadePuffer: The First Successful LLM-Driven Ransomware Attack - Dark Reading
items.summary: # JadePuffer: The First Complete LLM-Driven Ransomware Attack. An "agentic threat actor" successfully exploited a Langflow flaw to steal data from a production database server and encrypt other systems. The first documented case of an end-to-end ransomware operation executed autonomously by a large language model (LLM) has successfully performed extortion without a human operator, ushering in a new era in cyberattacks that has long been expected by security experts. Researchers at Sysdig discovered a campaign run by an "agentic threat actor" (ATA) they call JadePuffer, which exploited a flaw in an Internet-facing Langflow deployment and then pivoted to a production database server to run an adaptive and fully automated ransomware campaign, according to a recent report. First, JadePuffer exploited CVE-2025-3248, an unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability affecting Langflow, which is an open source tool for building AI applications. What's remarkable, however, is that these tactics were strung together by an AI model into a complete ransomware operation against an organization's exposed Internet-facing infrastructure, according to Sysdig.

items.title: Microsoft patches bug in video game Age of Empires II - TechCrunch
items.summary: # Microsoft patches bug in video game Age of Empires II. On Tuesday, Microsoft patched a historic record number of security bugs across its product lines, in large part due to the use of AI to help the company and external researchers discover bugs. Among the fixed vulnerabilities was one for the remastered version of the classic 25-year-old war strategy video game Age of Empires II. The flaw allowed hackers to take over a victim’s computer by sending a custom malicious game invite, according to security researchers. A video posted on X shows how the flaw could be exploited by hackers. According to cybersecurity firm Rapid7, a successful attack would have allowed hackers to place malicious files on the victim’s computer, opening the door for the hacker to achieve the ability to run malicious code on the victim’s machine. > Researchers at iFLYTEK have developed iFLYTEK-Embodied-Omni, a unified multimodal AI model that integrates vision, language, and action generation into a single framework. Unlike prior embodied agents which treat visual understanding, future state prediction, and action generation separately, their model uses shared multimodal self-attention to enable close coordination—analogous to a brain-cerebellum collaboration—between a vision-language "high-level brain" and an action-generating [...] action-generating "low-level cerebellum."
